page.layout: One page of text. Running head at top with page number at right. Two italic verse blocks, separated by a centred two-line heading. Below the Latin, a full-width German paragraph in black letter. Signature and catchword at the foot.

p.i: Si tibi sint nati, stimulabunt undique curae: Si non sunt, steriles sunt sine luce domus. Imprudens nescit, quid agat cum laude juventa: Deplorat Vires[?] saeva senecta suas. Optanda est igitur de binis altera rebus, Non nasci, aut natum morte perire citá.

main_text.head: EX METRODORI GRAECO EPIGRAMMATE; QVOD PRIORI contrarium.

p.i: Qualemcunque viam carpas, tibi consulo, vita: Magnum divûm[?] est spernere dona nefas.
Concio nobilitat linguas facunda disertas: Clamosum teritur non sine laude forum.
Suscipiunt dominos per gratam tecta quietem: Annuus à cultis est tibi fructus agris.
Turgida si terrent audaces aequora nautas, Spes lucri extinguit multiplicata metum.
Divitiæ[?] rebus sunt ornamenta secundis: Paupertas tacito tutior ipsa viro est.
Nupseris[?] aeternos germen tibi durat in annos: Expers conjugii est vita onerosa minus.
Fœcundos ornat natorum turba parentes: Non rodit steriles anxia cura domos.
Arma Vigens tractat multa cum laude juventa: Consiliis gaudet fera senecta suis.
Non ergo optanda est de binis altera rebus: Nam nasci, & natum morte perire licet.

p.bl: Welcher obstehenden / vnd mit dem Griechi-schen Text collationierten / Verß vngefehrliche Meynung in nachfolgende reimen gebracht wer-den kan / Die ein jeder nach seinem verstand vnnd vermögen verbessern mag:

page.notes: The first line of the Greek-epigram heading and the initial "Q" of "Qualemcunque" are a large woodcut-style initial, transcribed as Q joined to the word. "Vires" (line 4 of the first block) is unclear; the initial letter may be a special form of V. "Divûm" is read from a worn abbreviation mark and is doubtful. "Nupseris" is partly obscured in the scan. "Divitiæ" is doubtful at the ligature. The catchword "Leyds" is partly obscured by a flourish. A red pencil or ink underline appears under "Divitiæ" and "Paupertas"; it is not printed text and is not transcribed.
